sentences.text: Bifidobacterium dentium is a bifidobacterium of the mammalian gastrointestinal tract that shows acid resistance, adheres to human mucus and is concluded to be well adapted for commensalism in the gut.

It is also found in the mouth: a strain isolated from dental caries was sequenced, and the genus Bifidobacterium is reported to include Bifidobacterium dentium as an opportunistic cariogenic pathogen.

In germ-free mice monoassociated with live Bifidobacterium dentium, colonic expression of goblet cell markers and acidic mucin-filled goblet cells increased compared with heat-killed bacteria and germ-free controls.

Bifidobacterium dentium strains isolated from infant faeces metabolised the human milk oligosaccharides lacto-N-tetraose and lacto-N-neotetraose, consuming the galactose moiety and excreting lacto-N-triose.

A study reported Bifidobacterium dentium as enriched in faecal samples from patients with melanoma and colorectal cancer, with high intratumoral abundance correlating with poorer survival in colorectal cancer patients.
